config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is Android 17 only relevant to native Android apps?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No. The platform behavior directly affects native apps, but the same device trend affects web apps, PWAs, embedded WebViews, and responsive sites opened on Android tablets, foldables, and desktop-style windows. If your UI depends on a fixed phone-shaped viewport, Android 17 is a signal to retest it."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What viewport sizes should I test for Android foldables?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Test both the cover-display range and the unfolded main-display range. In practice, include narrow phone widths around 320-430 CSS px, medium widths around 600-840 CSS px, at least one landscape case, and at least one near-square case. Then compare against the current Android Viewport Sizes chart."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is screen resolution or viewport size more important for responsive design?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Viewport size is usually more important for layout because CSS media queries and most web layout decisions operate in CSS pixels. Screen resolution and DPR still matter for image sharpness, canvas rendering, and density-aware assets."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I test Android multi-window layouts without every device?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Use a responsive tester with custom viewport sizes, then validate critical flows on at least one real Android device or emulator. Multi-window testing is about resizing the available window, so custom widths and heights are more useful than relying only on named device presets."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I build separate layouts for every foldable model?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Usually no. Build adaptive components that respond to available width, height, and aspect ratio. Use device charts to understand the range of real values, then create content-based breakpoints instead of model-specific branches."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

      "name": "Should I use V-Sync with G-Sync/FreeSync?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "In NVIDIA Control Panel: Turn ON (acts as frame cap at top of VRR range) In-game: Turn OFF (prevents double-buffering lag) This combination gives you the best of both worlds: tear-free gaming within VRR range and smooth capping at max refresh."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the best response time setting?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Start at Medium/Normal, then test with testufo.com/ghosting. Increase if you see ghosting trails. Decrease if you see inverse ghosting (bright coronas). The \"1ms\" advertised often requires extreme overdrive that causes issues."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I use fullscreen or borderless window?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Competitive games: Exclusive fullscreen (lowest input lag) Casual/multitasking: Borderless windowed (alt-tab faster) Note: Windows 11 optimizations have reduced the difference significantly."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I know if my settings are working?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Use these tests: - Refresh rate: testufo.com (shows actual Hz) - G-Sync/FreeSync: NVIDIA Pendulum or VRR indicator in monitor OSD - Response time: testufo.com/ghosting - Input lag: Feel for responsiveness, or use NVIDIA Reflex"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is HDR worth enabling?",

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I know what resolution my monitor supports?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Check your monitor's specifications in the manual or manufacturer website. Most monitors display their native resolution in the product name (e.g., \"24-inch 1080p Monitor\"). You can also check in Windows Display Settings or Mac System Preferences where all supported resolutions are listed in the dropdown menu."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the difference between resolution and screen size?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Resolution is the number of pixels (e.g., 1920×1080), while screen size is the physical diagonal measurement in inches (e.g., 24\"). The same resolution can appear on different sized screens - a 1080p laptop screen looks much sharper than a 1080p TV because the pixels are packed more densely (higher PPI)."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I use the highest resolution my monitor supports?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Generally yes, use your monitor's native resolution for the sharpest image. However, consider performance: higher resolutions require more GPU power for gaming and may make text/UI elements very small, requiring scaling adjustments for comfortable viewing."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Why does my 4K monitor look blurry on Windows?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "This is usually due to scaling issues. 4K monitors at 100% scaling make everything tiny, so Windows automatically scales to 150-200%. Some older applications don't handle scaling well. Try adjusting scaling in Display Settings or enable \"Fix scaling for apps\" in Windows 10/11."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can I use different resolutions on multiple monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, modern operating systems handle different resolutions well. However, mouse movement between screens might feel inconsistent, and window dragging can be awkward if resolutions differ significantly. For best experience, try to match resolutions or at least aspect ratios."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What resolution should I use for streaming or recording?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "For streaming: 1080p 60fps is the most common. Use 720p 60fps for slower internet or 1440p if you have excellent upload speed. For recording: Use your native resolution for best quality, or 1080p for broader compatibility and smaller file sizes."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I change my resolution if I can't see the screen properly?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Boot into Safe Mode (Windows) or Recovery Mode (Mac) where lower resolutions are used by default. On Windows, you can also press Windows + P to cycle through display modes, or use Windows + I to open Settings and navigate to Display by keyboard. On Mac, reset NVRAM/PRAM by holding Option + Command + P + R during startup."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is higher resolution always better?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Not necessarily. Higher resolution provides more detail and screen space but requires more GPU power, makes text smaller (requiring scaling), and creates larger file sizes for content creation. The \"best\" resolution depends on your screen size, use case, graphics hardware, and viewing distance. ---"
      }
    },

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",

  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What is the most common laptop screen size?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "15.6 inches is the most common laptop screen size globally, accounting for approximately 40-50% of laptop sales. It offers the best balance between screen real estate, portability, cost, and component availability. The second most popular is 13.3-14 inches for ultraportable laptops."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I measure a laptop screen with a broken screen?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "If the screen is broken but display boundaries are still visible, measure the diagonal of the visible display area (not the bezel). If completely shattered, check your laptop model number on the bottom sticker or search online for your model's specifications. The screen size is almost always listed in official specs."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Does laptop screen size include the bezel?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No, laptop screen size does not include the bezel (frame). It only measures the active display area - the diagonal distance of the actual screen. This is why two laptops with the same screen size (e.g., 15.6\") can have different overall dimensions if one has thinner bezels."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can I replace my laptop screen with a different size?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Generally no. Laptop screens are specifically designed for each model. The screen size, mounting points, connector type, and cable length are model-specific. However, you can sometimes find screens with the same physical size but different resolution or panel type (IPS vs. TN) that are compatible. Always verify compatibility before purchasing."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the difference between laptop screen size and resolution?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Screen size is the physical diagonal measurement in inches (e.g., 15.6\"). Resolution is the number of pixels (e.g., 1920×1080). They're independent - the same 15.6\" screen can have 1366×768 (HD), 1920×1080 (Full HD), or 3840×2160 (4K) resolution. Higher resolution means sharper image but requires more GPU power."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is a 15.6\" laptop too big to carry?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "It depends on your needs and tolerance. A 15.6\" laptop typically weighs 4-5.5 lbs (1.8-2.5 kg) and fits in most backpacks. For daily commuting or frequent travel, 13-14\" is generally more comfortable. For occasional carry between home and office, 15.6\" is manageable. Consider a lightweight 15.6\" model (under 4 lbs) if you need the screen space but want better portability."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I measure a MacBook screen?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Measure exactly the same way as any laptop: diagonal distance from corner to corner of the active display area only, excluding the black bezel. MacBooks make this easy because the aluminum bezel is clearly distinct from the glass display. For recent models, the size is in the product name (MacBook Pro 14-inch, 16-inch, MacBook Air 13-inch)."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What laptop screen size is best for gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "15.6\" to 17.3\" is ideal for gaming laptops. 15.6\" offers the best balance - still somewhat portable, fits gaming hardware, large enough for immersion. 17.3\" provides maximum immersion but sacrifices portability. Screens smaller than 15\" often can't fit high-performance gaming components. Also consider high refresh rate (144Hz+) which is more important than size for competitive gaming. ---"
      }
    },
    {

config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do I measure the screen or the bezel?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Only measure the screen, not the bezel (frame). The advertised monitor size refers only to the visible display area, excluding the plastic or metal frame around it."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is monitor size measured diagonally?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, always diagonally, from one corner of the screen to the diagonally opposite corner. This is the industry standard for all monitors and TVs."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I measure a curved monitor?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Measure the straight-line diagonal distance, not following the curve. Use a ruler or tape measure and measure as if the screen were flat, from corner to corner in a straight line."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What if my measurement is between standard sizes?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Round to the nearest standard size. For example: - 23.5\"-23.9\" = 24\" monitor - 27.5\"-28\" = 27\" monitor - 31.5\"-32.5\" = 32\" monitor Manufacturers sometimes specify 23.8\" or 27.5\", but these are marketed as 24\" and 27\" respectively."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can I use my phone to measure monitor size?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, if you have a measuring app that uses your phone's camera and AR capabilities. Apps like \"Measure\" (iOS) or \"Measure\" (Android) can estimate dimensions. However, physical measurement is more accurate."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How do I measure an ultrawide monitor?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Same method: Measure diagonally from corner to corner. Ultrawide monitors have larger diagonal measurements (34\", 38\", 49\") but the measurement technique is identical."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the difference between monitor size and screen resolution?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Monitor size: Physical diagonal measurement (e.g., 27\") Screen resolution: Number of pixels (e.g., 2560×1440) They're independent: - Same size can have different resolutions - Same resolution can appear on different sizes"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How accurate does my measurement need to be?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Within ±0.5 inch is sufficient for most purposes. Manufacturers themselves have small variations (a \"27 inch\" might be 27.0\" or 27.5\"). Round to the nearest standard size for practical purposes. ---"
      }
    },
    {

}

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What size monitor should I buy for gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "For most gamers, 27 inches at 1440p is the sweet spot. It offers enough screen real estate for immersion without being too large to see the entire screen comfortably. For competitive esports, some prefer 24 inches at 1080p to see everything at a glance. If you sit further back or want maximum immersion, 32 inches at 4K works well."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is 4K worth it in 2025?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "It depends on your use case. For content creation, photo editing, and productivity with lots of text, 4K is excellent at 27\" or larger. For gaming, 4K requires a powerful GPU (RTX 4070 or better) to run smoothly at high refresh rates. For casual use and gaming on mid-range hardware, 1440p offers better value."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "IPS or VA for gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "IPS is generally better for most gaming due to faster response times and better color accuracy. Choose VA if you primarily play single-player games, watch movies, or game in a dark room where the superior contrast is noticeable. Avoid VA for competitive multiplayer due to potential black smearing."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How much should I spend on a monitor?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "A good rule is to spend 15-25% of your total PC budget on the monitor. For a $1000 PC, budget $150-250. For a $2000 PC, budget $300-500. Remember monitors last longer than other components, so it's worth investing in quality."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do I need G-Sync or FreeSync?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "FreeSync is free and works with both AMD and NVIDIA GPUs, making it the practical choice for most buyers. Hardware G-Sync (with the module) offers slightly better performance at the extreme low end of the refresh range, but the premium is only worth it for high-end setups with NVIDIA GPUs."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the best refresh rate for gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "144Hz is the sweet spot for most gamers - it's a huge improvement over 60Hz and achievable with mid-range GPUs. 240Hz offers diminishing returns unless you play competitive esports. 60Hz is only acceptable for single-player games or if you have a very weak GPU."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I buy a curved monitor?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Curved monitors are personal preference. They can provide a more immersive experience for gaming and help reduce eye strain on ultrawide displays. However, they're not ideal for professional work requiring straight lines (CAD, graphic design). For standard 16:9 monitors, flat is usually fine."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How long do monitors last?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Quality monitors typically last 5-10 years. LED backlights may dim over time, but modern monitors rarely fail outright. OLED panels may degrade faster due to organic materials, though this takes many years of heavy use. Buy quality and your monitor will outlast several PC upgrades. ---"
      }
    },

config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Betrifft Android 17 nur native Android-Apps?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Nein. Die Plattformänderung betrifft direkt native Apps. Der gleiche Gerätetrend betrifft aber auch Web-Apps, PWAs, WebViews und responsive Websites, die auf Android-Tablets, Foldables und Desktop-ähnlichen Fenstern geöffnet werden. Wenn dein UI von einem festen Smartphone-Viewport ausgeht, solltest du es neu testen."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Welche Viewport-Größen sollte ich für Android-Foldables testen?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Teste Cover-Display und aufgeklapptes Hauptdisplay. Praktisch heißt das: 320-430 CSS px für schmale Smartphone-Breiten, 600-840 CSS px für mittlere Breiten, mindestens ein Querformat mit knapper Höhe und mindestens ein fast quadratisches Szenario. Vergleiche danach mit der aktuellen Tabelle Android Viewport-Größen."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Ist Bildschirmauflösung oder Viewport-Größe wichtiger für Responsive Design?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Für Layouts ist meistens die Viewport-Größe wichtiger, weil CSS Media Queries und Layoutentscheidungen in CSS-Pixeln arbeiten. Bildschirmauflösung und DPR bleiben wichtig für Bildschärfe, Canvas-Rendering und dichteabhängige Assets."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Wie teste ich Android Multi-Window ohne jedes Gerät?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Nutze zuerst einen Responsive Tester mit Custom-Viewport-Größen und prüfe danach kritische Flows auf mindestens einem echten Android-Gerät oder Emulator. Multi-Window-Testing bedeutet, das verfügbare Fenster im Mehrfenstermodus zu verändern; benannte Geräte-Presets reichen dafür nicht aus."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Welche Größen sind für Android-17-Multi-Window besonders wichtig?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Teste mindestens 360, 390, 412, 600, 768, 840 und 1024 CSS px. Ergänze 720 x 720 für ein fast quadratisches Foldable-Szenario und 844 x 390 für Querformat mit knapper Höhe. Damit deckst du die meisten kritischen Übergänge zwischen Smartphone, Foldable, Tablet, Split-Screen und Desktop-Fenster ab."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Muss ich für jedes Foldable-Modell ein eigenes Layout bauen?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "In der Regel nein. Baue adaptive Komponenten, die auf verfügbare Breite, Höhe und Seitenverhältnis reagieren. Gerätetabellen helfen, reale Wertebereiche zu verstehen; die eigentlichen Breakpoints sollten aus Inhalt und Nutzerflow entstehen, nicht aus einzelnen Modellnamen."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Android 17 afecta solo a apps Android nativas?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No. El cambio de plataforma afecta directamente a apps nativas. Pero la misma tendencia de dispositivos también afecta a web apps, PWAs, WebViews y sitios responsive que se abren en tablets Android, plegables y ventanas de estilo escritorio. Si tu UI depende de un viewport fijo con forma de teléfono, conviene volver a probarla."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué tamaños de viewport debo probar para plegables Android?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Prueba la pantalla externa y la pantalla principal desplegada. En la práctica, eso significa 320-430 CSS px para anchos estrechos de smartphone, 600-840 CSS px para anchos medios, al menos un horizontal con poca altura y al menos un escenario casi cuadrado. Después compara con la tabla actual de tamaños de viewport Android."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Es más importante la resolución de pantalla o el tamaño de viewport para responsive design?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para layouts, normalmente importa más el tamaño de viewport, porque CSS media queries y la mayoría de decisiones de layout trabajan en píxeles CSS. El tamaño de pantalla reportado por el navegador, la resolución física del panel y el DPR siguen siendo útiles para nitidez de imagen, renderizado de canvas y assets dependientes de densidad."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿600 CSS px es lo mismo que 600 dp en Android?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No. Android dp pertenece al sistema de layouts nativos y reglas de plataforma. CSS px es la unidad que ve una página web en el viewport. En este artículo, 600 y 840 CSS px son anchos de prueba web, no conversiones directas desde Android dp."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Cómo pruebo layouts Android multiventana sin tener todos los dispositivos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Usa primero un responsive tester con tamaños de viewport personalizados y después valida los flujos críticos en al menos un dispositivo Android real o emulador. Probar multiventana significa cambiar la ventana disponible; los presets con nombre de dispositivo no bastan para eso."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué tamaños son especialmente importantes para Android 17 multiventana?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Prueba al menos 360, 390, 412, 600, 768, 840 y 1024 CSS px. Añade 720 x 720 para un escenario plegable casi cuadrado y 844 x 390 para horizontal con poca altura. Así cubres la mayoría de transiciones críticas entre smartphone, plegable, tablet, split-screen y ventana de escritorio."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Debo construir un layout separado para cada modelo plegable?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Normalmente no. Construye componentes adaptativos que respondan al ancho disponible, la altura y la relación de aspecto. Las tablas de dispositivos ayudan a entender rangos reales; los breakpoints deberían salir del contenido y del flujo de usuario, no de nombres de modelo individuales."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "O Android 17 afeta apenas apps Android nativos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Não. A mudança de plataforma afeta diretamente apps nativos. Mas a mesma tendência de dispositivos também afeta web apps, PWAs, WebViews e sites responsivos abertos em tablets Android, dobráveis e janelas de estilo desktop. Se sua UI depende de um viewport fixo em formato de telefone, vale a pena testar novamente."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Quais tamanhos de viewport devo testar para dobráveis Android?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Teste a tela externa e a tela principal desdobrada. Na prática, isso significa 320-430 CSS px para larguras estreitas de smartphone, 600-840 CSS px para larguras médias, pelo menos um cenário em paisagem com pouca altura e pelo menos um cenário quase quadrado. Depois compare com a tabela atual de tamanhos de viewport Android."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Resolução de tela ou tamanho do viewport é mais importante para design responsivo?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para layouts, normalmente o tamanho do viewport é mais importante, porque CSS media queries e a maioria das decisões de layout web trabalham em pixels CSS. O tamanho de tela reportado pelo navegador, a resolução física do painel e o DPR continuam úteis para nitidez de imagem, renderização em canvas e ativos dependentes de densidade."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "600 CSS px é o mesmo que 600 dp no Android?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Não. Android dp pertence ao sistema de layouts nativos e regras de plataforma. CSS px é a unidade que uma página web vê no viewport. Neste artigo, 600 e 840 CSS px são larguras de teste web, não conversões diretas a partir de Android dp."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Como testar layouts Android multijanela sem ter todos os dispositivos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Use primeiro um responsive tester com tamanhos de viewport personalizados e depois valide fluxos críticos em pelo menos um dispositivo Android real ou emulador. Testar multijanela significa alterar a janela disponível; presets com nome de dispositivo não bastam para isso."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Quais tamanhos são especialmente importantes para Android 17 multijanela?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Teste pelo menos 360, 390, 412, 600, 768, 840 e 1024 CSS px. Adicione 720 x 720 para um cenário dobrável quase quadrado e 844 x 390 para paisagem com pouca altura. Assim você cobre a maioria das transições críticas entre smartphone, dobrável, tablet, modo de tela dividida e janela desktop."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Devo criar um layout separado para cada modelo dobrável?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Normalmente não. Crie componentes adaptativos que respondam à largura disponível, à altura e à proporção de tela. As tabelas de dispositivos ajudam a entender intervalos reais; os breakpoints devem vir do conteúdo e do fluxo do usuário, não de nomes de modelos específicos."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Non. Le changement de plateforme touche directement les apps natives. Si votre UI dépend d'un viewport fixe en forme de téléphone, il faut la retester."

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Quelles tailles de viewport tester pour les pliables Android ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Testez l'écran externe et l'écran principal déplié. En pratique, cela signifie 320-430 CSS px pour les largeurs étroites de smartphone, 600-840 CSS px pour les largeurs moyennes, au moins un scénario paysage avec peu de hauteur et au moins un scénario presque carré. Comparez ensuite avec le tableau actuel des tailles de viewport Android."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Résolution d'écran ou taille du viewport : qu'est-ce qui compte le plus pour le design responsive ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Pour les layouts, la taille du viewport est généralement plus importante, car les media queries CSS et la plupart des décisions de layout web travaillent en pixels CSS. La taille d'écran signalée par le navigateur, la résolution physique de la dalle et le DPR restent utiles pour la netteté des images, le rendu canvas et les ressources dépendantes de la densité."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "600 CSS px est-il équivalent à 600 dp sur Android ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Non. Le dp Android appartient au système de layouts natifs et aux règles de plateforme. Le pixel CSS est l'unité qu'une page web voit dans le viewport. Dans cet article, 600 et 840 CSS px sont des largeurs de test web, pas des conversions directes depuis les dp Android."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Comment tester les layouts Android multifenêtre sans posséder tous les appareils ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Utilisez d'abord un testeur responsive avec des tailles de viewport personnalisées, puis validez les flux critiques sur au moins un appareil Android réel ou un émulateur. Tester le multifenêtre signifie modifier la fenêtre disponible ; les presets nommés par appareil ne suffisent pas."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Quelles tailles sont particulièrement importantes pour Android 17 en multifenêtre ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Testez au moins 360, 390, 412, 600, 768, 840 et 1024 CSS px. Ajoutez 720 x 720 pour un scénario pliable presque carré et 844 x 390 pour un paysage avec peu de hauteur. Vous couvrez ainsi la plupart des transitions critiques entre smartphone, pliable, tablette, écran partagé et fenêtre desktop."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Faut-il créer un layout séparé pour chaque modèle pliable ?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "En général, non. Créez des composants adaptatifs qui répondent à la largeur disponible, à la hauteur et au rapport d'aspect. Les tableaux d'appareils aident à comprendre les plages réelles ; les breakpoints doivent venir du contenu et du flux utilisateur, pas des noms de modèles."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 inches is better for pure competitive FPS gaming (CS2, Valorant) because the full screen is easier to scan quickly. 27 inches is better for balanced gaming that mixes competitive and casual FPS titles, offering better detail and immersion while staying manageable."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Why do many competitive players use small monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Many competitive players use 24 25 inch monitors because the whole screen is easier to keep in view without head movement. That makes HUD checks, corner checks, and target tracking feel more predictable during fast rounds."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Is 32 inch too big for FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, 32 inches is often too large for close range competitive FPS gaming. It can work if you sit farther back, but at a typical desk distance it usually requires more scanning than 24\" or 27\". It is a better fit for casual FPS, controller campaigns, 4K single player games, and mixed work setups."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What monitor size do most FPS pros use?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Most serious FPS setups cluster around 24 25 inch high refresh monitors, while many mixed use players choose 27 inch 1440p. Larger monitors are better treated as casual, campaign, streaming, or multi purpose displays rather than the default competitive choice."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I get 1080p or 1440p for FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "For 24 inch competitive FPS, 1080p at 240Hz+ is the easiest path to high frame rates. For 27 inch balanced gaming, 1440p at 165Hz+ offers better image detail while staying practical for many modern PCs."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "How far should I sit from my gaming monitor?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "For 24 inch: 20 24 inches (51 61cm). For 27 inch: 24 28 inches (61 71cm). For 32 inch: 30 36 inches (76 91cm). Sitting closer than optimal causes eye strain; sitting further reduces competitive advantage and immersion."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can I use a TV for FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "TVs (40\"+) are not recommended for competitive FPS gaming due to excessive size causing slow target acquisition, typically higher input lag (even in game mode), and viewing distance challenges. TVs are acceptable for casual couch gaming but put you at a significant disadvantage in competitive play."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What's the best refresh rate for FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Minimum: 144Hz. Recommended for competitive play: 240Hz if your PC can sustain it. High end: 360Hz+ for players who already have strong frame pacing and low system latency. The jump from 60Hz to 144Hz is large; higher refresh rates are smaller refinements."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

For most gamers, flat 27\" monitors offer the best versatility."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do curved monitors cause eye strain?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No, curved monitors typically reduce eye strain compared to flat monitors. The curve matches natural eye curvature, reduces eye movement across the screen, and maintains consistent viewing distance. However, some users need 1 2 weeks to adapt to the curvature initially."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Are curved monitors good for competitive gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Generally no. 98%+ of professional competitive gamers use flat monitors because curved monitors can introduce subtle geometry distortion that affects aim precision. Tournaments exclusively use flat monitors, so competitive players should train on flat displays for consistency."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What size monitor should be curved vs flat?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 27\": Always flat (curvature benefit minimal). 32\": Either works, slight preference curved. 34\" ultrawide: Strongly recommend curved. 49\" super ultrawide: Curved essential. The larger the monitor, the more beneficial curvature becomes."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do curved monitors distort the image?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, slightly. Curved monitors introduce subtle geometric distortion where straight lines may appear slightly curved, especially at screen edges. This is usually not noticeable in games but can affect productivity work, web browsing, and competitive gaming precision."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Are curved monitors worth the extra cost?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Only in specific scenarios: 32\"+ monitors for immersive gaming, ultrawide monitors (essential), sim racing setups. For 24 27\" monitors or competitive gaming, the premium isn't justified. Curved provides real benefits for the right use cases but isn't universally better."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can you wall mount curved monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, but with limitations. Curved monitors don't sit flush against walls and require more depth clearance. Special mounting arms may be needed. Flat monitors are much easier to wall mount and more space efficient."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do streamers prefer curved or flat monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Most streamers prefer flat monitors because they record better on camera, provide standard viewer perspective, and offer better versatility for various content types. Curved monitors can create video distortion and are harder to frame properly for streaming setups."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Can I use an ultrawide monitor for competitive FPS games?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {

      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "What GPU do I need for ultrawide gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "For 3440×1440 (21:9) at 60 FPS: RTX 4060 Ti minimum. For 144 FPS: RTX 4070 or better. For 5120×1440 (32:9) at 60 FPS: RTX 4070. For 144 FPS: RTX 4080 or 4090. Ultrawide requires 34 100% more GPU power than standard 1440p."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Are ultrawide monitors worth it in 2025?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Yes, if you primarily play single player games, do content creation, or value immersive experiences. Not worth it if you play competitive FPS, stream regularly, or need true multitasking. Consider your primary use case—ultrawides excel at specific tasks but aren't universally better."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Should I get a 34\" ultrawide or dual 27\" monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "34\" ultrawide if: immersive gaming, video editing, programming, clean aesthetics. Dual 27\" if: competitive gaming, streaming, multitasking, flexibility. Budget: dual 27\" can be cheaper ($700 vs $500 800). Performance: ultrawide needs better GPU."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Do all games support ultrawide monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No. About 85% of modern AAA games fully support 21:9. Most competitive FPS don't (CS2, Valorant locked to 16:9). 32:9 support is ~45%. Older games and some console ports lack support. Community mods exist but aren't recommended for online games."
      }

      "name": "Can I use a 49\" ultrawide as two monitors?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {

        "text": "Yes, most 49\" ultrawide monitors have Picture by Picture (PbP) mode that treats them as two separate displays. However, you'll have a bezel free split in the middle. Better than physical bezel but not true dual monitors. Windows treats it as one or two displays depending on mode."

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Which is better for productivity: ultrawide or dual monitors?",

      }
    }

config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "超宽屏比双显示器更适合游戏吗？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "对于沉浸式单机游戏，是的——超宽屏提供无边框的无缝电影体验。对于竞技游戏和多任务处理，双显示器更好，因为16:9兼容性、用于Discord/指南的副屏幕和更高刷新率可用性。85%的游戏支持超宽屏，但竞技游戏通常不支持。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "我可以使用超宽屏显示器玩竞技FPS游戏吗？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "大多数竞技FPS游戏要么不支持超宽屏（CS2、无畏契约），要么额外的FOV被认为是劣势。99%的职业选手使用标准16:9显示器。超宽屏在锦标赛中被禁止。对于休闲竞技游戏，一些游戏如使命召唤和Apex有效，但你可能处于劣势。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "超宽屏游戏需要什么GPU？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "对于3440×1440（21:9）60 FPS：最低RTX 4060 Ti。144 FPS：RTX 4070或更好。对于5120×1440（32:9）60 FPS：RTX 4070。144 FPS：RTX 4080或4090。超宽屏需要比标准1440p多34 100%的GPU算力。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "2025年超宽屏显示器值得吗？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "是的，如果你主要玩单机游戏、从事内容创作或重视沉浸式体验。如果你玩竞技FPS、定期直播或需要真正的多任务处理，则不值得。考虑你的主要用例——超宽屏在特定任务中出色，但并非普遍更好。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "我应该买34英寸超宽屏还是双27英寸显示器？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "34英寸超宽屏如果：沉浸式游戏、视频编辑、编程、简洁美学。双27英寸如果：竞技游戏、直播、多任务处理、灵活性。预算：双27英寸可能更便宜（¥4900 vs ¥3500 5600）。性能：超宽屏需要更好的GPU。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "所有游戏都支持超宽屏显示器吗？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "不。约85%的现代3A游戏完全支持21:9。大多数竞技FPS不支持（CS2、无畏契约锁定为16:9）。32:9支持约45%。老游戏和一些主机移植缺乏支持。存在社区Mod但不推荐用于在线游戏。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "我可以将49英寸超宽屏用作两个显示器吗？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "是的，大多数49英寸超宽屏显示器有画中画（PbP）模式，将它们视为两个单独的显示器。但是，你会在中间有一个无边框分割。比物理边框好，但不是真正的双显示器。Windows根据模式将其视为一个或两个显示器。"
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "哪个更适合生产力：超宽屏还是双显示器？",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "取决于工作流程。超宽屏更好：编程、视频编辑、无缝工作流程、简洁美学。双显示器更好：视频通话+工作、完全分离的应用程序、混合方向（横向+纵向）、窗口管理。最有生产力：49英寸超宽屏或三显示器，但对许多人来说过度。"
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

Flat Monitore sind besser für Competitive Gaming (null Verzerrung, Tournament Standard, präzises Zielen), während curved Monitore bei immersivem Einzelspieler Gaming glänzen (besseres FOV, reduzierte Augenbelastung, cinematischer). Für die meisten Gamer bieten flat 27\" Monitore die beste Vielseitigkeit."
      }
    },

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Verursachen curved Monitore Augenbelastung?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Nein, curved Monitore reduzieren typischerweise Augenbelastung verglichen mit flat Monitoren. Die Kurve entspricht natürlicher Augenkrümmung, reduziert Augenbewegung über Bildschirm und behält konsistenten Betrachtungsabstand. Jedoch benötigen manche Nutzer 1 2 Wochen um sich an die Krümmung zu gewöhnen."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Sind curved Monitore gut für Competitive Gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Generell nein. 98%+ professioneller Competitive Gamer verwenden flat Monitore, da curved Monitore subtile Geometrie Verzerrung einführen können, die Ziel Präzision beeinflusst. Turniere verwenden ausschließlich flat Monitore, daher sollten competitive Spieler auf flat Displays trainieren für Konsistenz."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Welche Monitor-Größe sollte curved vs flat sein?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 27\": Immer flat (Krümmungsvorteil minimal). 32\": Beides funktioniert, leichte Präferenz für curved. 34\" Ultrawide: Stark curved empfohlen. 49\" Super Ultrawide: Curved essentiell. Je größer der Monitor, desto vorteilhafter wird Krümmung."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Verzerren curved Monitore das Bild?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Ja, leicht. Curved Monitore führen subtile geometrische Verzerrung ein, wo gerade Linien leicht gekrümmt erscheinen können, besonders an Bildschirmrändern. Dies ist meist nicht bemerkbar in Spielen, kann aber Produktivitätsarbeit, Web Browsing und Competitive Gaming Präzision beeinträchtigen."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Sind curved Monitore die zusätzlichen Kosten wert?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Nur in spezifischen Szenarien: 32\"+ Monitore für immersives Gaming, Ultrawide Monitore (essentiell), Sim Racing Setups. Für 24 27\" Monitore oder Competitive Gaming ist der Aufpreis nicht gerechtfertigt. Curved bietet echte Vorteile für richtige Anwendungsfälle, ist aber nicht universell besser."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

        "text": "Für immersives Einzelspieler Gaming, ja—Ultrawide bietet nahtloses, kinoreifes Erlebnis ohne Bezels.       "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Die meisten kompetitiven FPS Spiele unterstützen entweder kein Ultrawide (CS2, Valorant) oder das extra FOV wird als Nachteil betrachtet. 99% der professionellen Spieler nutzen Standard 16:9 Monitore. Ultrawides sind Turnier verboten. Für casual kompetitives Spiel funktionieren manche Spiele wie COD und Apex, aber Sie könnten im Nachteil sein."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Welche GPU brauche ich für Ultrawide-Gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Für 3440×1440 (21:9) bei 60 FPS: RTX 4060 Ti minimum. Für 144 FPS: RTX 4070 oder besser. Für 5120×1440 (32:9) bei 60 FPS: RTX 4070. Für 144 FPS: RTX 4080 oder 4090. Ultrawide benötigt 34 100% mehr GPU Power als Standard 1440p."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Sind Ultrawide-Monitore 2025 ihr Geld wert?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Ja, wenn Sie primär Einzelspieler Spiele spielen, Content Erstellung betreiben oder immersive Erfahrungen schätzen. Nicht wert wenn Sie kompetitive FPS spielen, regelmäßig streamen oder echtes Multitasking brauchen. Betrachten Sie Ihren primären Anwendungsfall—Ultrawides glänzen bei spezifischen Aufgaben, sind aber nicht universell besser."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Sollte ich einen 34\" Ultrawide oder Dual 27\" Monitore bekommen?",

    },

      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Unterstützen alle Spiele Ultrawide-Monitore?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",

      "name": "Welches ist besser für Produktivität: Ultrawide oder Dual-Monitore?",

      }
    }

  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Es mejor 24 o 27 pulgadas para FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 pulgadas es mejor para FPS puramente competitivo (CS2, Valorant) porque toda la pantalla se escanea más rápido. 27 pulgadas es mejor para un uso equilibrado que mezcla FPS competitivos y casuales, con más detalle e inmersión sin perder control."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Por qué muchos jugadores competitivos usan monitores pequeños?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Muchos jugadores competitivos usan monitores de 24 25 pulgadas porque toda la pantalla queda más fácil de ver sin mover la cabeza. El minimapa, las esquinas, el HUD y el seguimiento de objetivos se sienten más predecibles."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Es 32 pulgadas demasiado grande para FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sí, 32 pulgadas suele ser demasiado grande para FPS competitivo de escritorio si te sientas cerca. Puede funcionar con más distancia, pero en un escritorio típico exige más escaneo que 24 o 27 pulgadas. Encaja mejor con FPS casual, campañas con mando, 4K single player y uso mixto."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué tamaño de monitor usan la mayoría de pros de FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Los setups FPS serios suelen concentrarse en 24 25 pulgadas de alto refresco, mientras muchos jugadores mixtos eligen 27 pulgadas 1440p. Los monitores más grandes encajan mejor con uso casual, campañas, streaming o uso multiuso que como opción competitiva por defecto."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Debería obtener 1080p o 1440p para FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para FPS competitivo en 24 pulgadas, 1080p a 240Hz+ es la ruta más fácil hacia FPS altos. Para gaming equilibrado en 27 pulgadas, 1440p a 165Hz+ ofrece más detalle y sigue siendo realista para muchos PCs modernos."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué tan lejos debería sentarme de mi monitor gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para 24 pulgadas: 51 61cm. Para 27 pulgadas: 61 71cm. Para 32 pulgadas: 76 91cm. Sentarse más cerca que lo óptimo causa fatiga ocular; sentarse más lejos reduce ventaja competitiva e inmersión."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Cuál es la mejor tasa de refresco para FPS gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Mínimo: 144Hz. Para competitivo: 240Hz si tu PC puede sostener FPS cercanos. Gama alta: 360Hz+ para quien ya resolvió frame pacing y latencia del sistema. El salto de 60Hz a 144Hz es grande; los saltos posteriores son refinamientos menores."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Es un monitor curvo o plano mejor para gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Depende del estilo gaming. Los monitores planos son mejores para gaming competitivo (cero distorsión, estándar torneo, puntería precisa), mientras los monitores curvos sobresalen en gaming inmersivo un jugador (mejor FOV, fatiga ocular reducida, más cinemático). Para la mayoría de gamers, los monitores planos 27\" ofrecen la mejor versatilidad."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Los monitores curvos causan fatiga ocular?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No, los monitores curvos típicamente reducen fatiga ocular comparado con monitores planos. La curva coincide con curvatura ocular natural, reduce movimiento ocular a través pantalla y mantiene distancia visualización consistente. Sin embargo, algunos usuarios necesitan 1 2 semanas para adaptarse a la curvatura inicialmente."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Son buenos los monitores curvos para gaming competitivo?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Generalmente no. 98%+ de gamers competitivos profesionales usan monitores planos porque los monitores curvos pueden introducir distorsión geométrica sutil que afecta precisión puntería. Los torneos usan exclusivamente monitores planos, así que jugadores competitivos deberían entrenar en displays planos para consistencia."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué tamaño monitor debería ser curvo vs plano?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 27\": Siempre plano (beneficio curvatura mínimo). 32\": Cualquiera funciona, preferencia leve por curvo. 34\" ultrawide: Fuertemente recomendado curvo. 49\" super ultrawide: Curvo esencial. Mientras más grande el monitor, más beneficiosa se vuelve la curvatura."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Los monitores curvos distorsionan la imagen?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sí, ligeramente. Los monitores curvos introducen distorsión geométrica sutil donde líneas rectas pueden aparecer ligeramente curvadas, especialmente en bordes pantalla. Esto usualmente no es notable en juegos pero puede afectar trabajo productividad, navegación web y precisión gaming competitivo."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Valen los monitores curvos el costo extra?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Solo en escenarios específicos: monitores 32\"+ para gaming inmersivo, monitores ultrawide (esencial), setups sim racing. Para monitores 24 27\" o gaming competitivo, la prima no está justificada. Curvo proporciona beneficios reales para casos uso correctos pero no es universalmente mejor."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Es ultrawide mejor que monitores duales para gaming?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para gaming inmersivo de un jugador, sí—ultrawide proporciona experiencia cinemática continua sin biseles. Para gaming competitivo y multitarea, los monitores duales son mejores debido a compatibilidad 16:9, pantalla secundaria para Discord/guías y disponibilidad de mayor tasa de refresco. 85% de juegos soportan ultrawide, pero títulos competitivos a menudo no."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Puedo usar un monitor ultrawide para juegos FPS competitivos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "La mayoría de juegos FPS competitivos o no soportan ultrawide (CS2, Valorant) o el FOV extra se considera una desventaja. 99% de jugadores profesionales usan monitores 16:9 estándar. Los ultrawides están prohibidos en torneos. Para juego competitivo casual, algunos juegos como COD y Apex funcionan, pero puedes estar en desventaja."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Qué GPU necesito para gaming ultrawide?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para 3440×1440 (21:9) a 60 FPS: RTX 4060 Ti mínimo. Para 144 FPS: RTX 4070 o mejor. Para 5120×1440 (32:9) a 60 FPS: RTX 4070. Para 144 FPS: RTX 4080 o 4090. Ultrawide requiere 34 100% más poder de GPU que 1440p estándar."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Valen la pena los monitores ultrawide en 2025?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sí, si principalmente juegas juegos de un jugador, haces creación de contenido o valoras experiencias inmersivas. No vale la pena si juegas FPS competitivos, haces stream regularmente o necesitas verdadera multitarea. Considera tu caso de uso principal—los ultrawides sobresalen en tareas específicas pero no son universalmente mejores."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Debería obtener un 34\" ultrawide o monitores duales 27\"?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "34\" ultrawide si: gaming inmersivo, edición de video, programación, estética limpia. Dual 27\" si: gaming competitivo, streaming, multitarea, flexibilidad. Presupuesto: dual 27\" puede ser más barato ($700 vs $500 800). Rendimiento: ultrawide necesita mejor GPU."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Todos los juegos soportan monitores ultrawide?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "No. Aproximadamente 85% de juegos AAA modernos soportan completamente 21:9. La mayoría de FPS competitivos no (CS2, Valorant bloqueado a 16:9). Soporte 32:9 es ~45%. Juegos antiguos y algunos ports de consola carecen de soporte. Existen mods de comunidad pero no se recomiendan para juegos en línea."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "¿Cuál es mejor para productividad: ultrawide o monitores duales?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Depende del flujo de trabajo. Ultrawide mejor para: coding, edición de video, flujos de trabajo continuos, estética limpia. Monitores duales mejor para: video llamadas + trabajo, aplicaciones completamente separadas, orientaciones mixtas (horizontal + vertical), gestión de ventanas. Más productivo: 49\" ultrawide o monitores triples, pero excesivo para muchos."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "24 ou 27 polegadas é melhor para FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 polegadas é melhor para FPS puramente competitivo (CS2, Valorant) porque a tela inteira é mais fácil de ler rapidamente. 27 polegadas é melhor para uso equilibrado que mistura FPS competitivo e casual, com mais detalhe e imersão sem perder controle."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Por que muitos jogadores competitivos usam monitores pequenos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Muitos jogadores competitivos usam monitores de 24 25 polegadas porque a tela inteira fica mais fácil de manter no campo de visão sem mover a cabeça. Minimapa, cantos, HUD e rastreamento de alvo ficam mais previsíveis."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "32 polegadas é muito grande para jogos FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sim, 32 polegadas costuma ser grande demais para FPS competitivo de mesa se você senta perto. Pode funcionar com maior distância, mas em uma mesa típica exige mais escaneamento que 24 ou 27 polegadas. Combina melhor com FPS casual, campanhas com controle, 4K single player e uso misto."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Qual tamanho de monitor a maioria dos profissionais de FPS usa?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Setups FPS sérios normalmente ficam em 24 25 polegadas com alto refresh, enquanto muitos jogadores mistos escolhem 27 polegadas 1440p. Monitores maiores fazem mais sentido para casual, campanha, streaming ou uso multiuso do que como padrão competitivo."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Devo pegar 1080p ou 1440p para jogos FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para FPS competitivo em 24 polegadas, 1080p a 240Hz+ é o caminho mais fácil para FPS alto. Para jogos equilibrados em 27 polegadas, 1440p a 165Hz+ oferece mais detalhe e ainda é realista para muitos PCs modernos."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "A que distância devo sentar do meu monitor gamer?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Para 24 polegadas: 20 24 polegadas (51 61cm). Para 27 polegadas: 24 28 polegadas (61 71cm). Para 32 polegadas: 30 36 polegadas (76 91cm). Sentar mais perto do que o ideal causa tensão ocular; sentar mais longe reduz vantagem competitiva e imersão."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Posso usar uma TV para jogos FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "TVs (40\"+) não são recomendadas para jogos FPS competitivos devido ao tamanho excessivo causando aquisição de alvos lenta, tipicamente maior latência de entrada (mesmo no modo jogo) e desafios de distância de visualização. TVs são aceitáveis para jogos casuais no sofá, mas colocam você em desvantagem significativa no jogo competitivo."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Qual é a melhor taxa de atualização para jogos FPS?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Mínimo: 144Hz. Para competitivo: 240Hz se seu PC sustenta FPS próximos. High end: 360Hz+ para quem já resolveu frame pacing e latência do sistema. O salto de 60Hz para 144Hz é grande; acima disso os ganhos são refinamentos menores."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

config.faq_structured_data:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "FAQPage",
  "mainEntity": [
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Um monitor curvo ou plano é melhor para jogos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Depende do estilo de jogo. Monitores planos são melhores para jogos competitivos (zero distorção, padrão de torneio, mira precisa), enquanto monitores curvos se destacam em jogos imersivos single player (melhor FOV, tensão ocular reduzida, mais cinemático). Para a maioria dos jogadores, monitores planos de 27\" oferecem a melhor versatilidade."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Monitores curvos causam tensão ocular?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Não, monitores curvos tipicamente reduzem a tensão ocular comparados aos monitores planos. A curva combina com a curvatura natural do olho, reduz o movimento ocular através da tela e mantém a distância de visualização consistente. No entanto, alguns usuários precisam de 1 2 semanas para se adaptar à curvatura inicialmente."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Monitores curvos são bons para jogos competitivos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Geralmente não. 98%+ dos jogadores competitivos profissionais usam monitores planos porque monitores curvos podem introduzir distorção geométrica sutil que afeta a precisão da mira. Torneios usam exclusivamente monitores planos, então jogadores competitivos devem treinar em telas planas para consistência."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Qual tamanho de monitor deve ser curvo vs plano?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "24 27\": Sempre plano (benefício da curvatura mínimo). 32\": Qualquer um funciona, leve preferência por curvo. 34\" ultrawide: Fortemente recomendado curvo. 49\" super ultrawide: Essencial curvo. Quanto maior o monitor, mais benéfica a curvatura se torna."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Monitores curvos distorcem a imagem?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sim, levemente. Monitores curvos introduzem distorção geométrica sutil onde linhas retas podem parecer levemente curvas, especialmente nas bordas da tela. Isso geralmente não é perceptível em jogos, mas pode afetar trabalho de produtividade, navegação na web e precisão de jogos competitivos."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Monitores curvos valem o custo extra?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Apenas em cenários específicos: monitores de 32\"+ para jogos imersivos, monitores ultrawide (essencial), configurações de sim racing. Para monitores de 24 27\" ou jogos competitivos, o prêmio não é justificado. Curvo fornece benefícios reais para os casos de uso certos, mas não é universalmente melhor."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Você pode montar monitores curvos na parede?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "Sim, mas com limitações. Monitores curvos não ficam nivelados contra paredes e requerem mais espaço de profundidade. Braços de montagem especiais podem ser necessários. Monitores planos são muito mais fáceis de montar na parede e mais eficientes em espaço."
      }
    },
    {
      "@type": "Question",
      "name": "Streamers preferem monitores curvos ou planos?",
      "acceptedAnswer": {
        "@type": "Answer",
        "text": "A maioria dos streamers prefere monitores planos porque gravam melhor na câmera, fornecem perspectiva padrão do espectador e oferecem melhor versatilidade para vários tipos de conteúdo. Monitores curvos podem criar distorção de vídeo e são mais difíceis de enquadrar corretamente para configurações de streaming."
      }
    }
  ]
}
</script>

sections.title: Dark-room viewing
sections.text: Use the black field when a bright browser window would distract from a movie, presentation, photo setup, or other low-light task. It changes the displayed pixels but does not turn off the monitor.

sections.title: Black level and backlight bleed

sections.title: OLED and LCD behavior
sections.text: OLED creates black by reducing or switching off individual pixel emission. LCD black depends on the panel blocking a still-active backlight, so some glow or lifted black can remain.

faqs.q: Does a black screen always save power?
faqs.a: No. Black may reduce power on some OLED devices. LCD backlights can stay active. Brightness, settings, and the rest of the interface also affect consumption.

faqs.q: How can I check for backlight bleed?
faqs.a: View the black field in a dim room at your normal brightness and distance. Inspect the edges and corners for uneven glow. Do not press the panel.

faqs.q: Does this page turn the monitor off?

sections.title: 暗室观看
sections.text: 在电影、演示、摄影布景或其他低光任务中，黑色区域不会像明亮浏览器窗口那样分散注意力。它只改变像素，并不会关闭显示器。

sections.title: 检查黑位和漏光
sections.text: 在昏暗房间以日常亮度观看，留意角落光晕、云状斑块、边缘漏光以及仍带颜色的像素。需要多种图案时可使用液晶屏幕测试器。

sections.title: OLED 与 LCD 的差异
sections.text: OLED 可降低或关闭单个像素的发光来显示黑色。LCD 需要遮住仍在工作的背光，因此可能出现光晕或偏亮的黑位。

faqs.q: 黑色屏幕一定省电吗？
faqs.a: 不一定。黑色可能让部分 OLED 设备降低功耗，而 LCD 背光仍可能保持开启；亮度、设置和其他界面也会影响耗电。

faqs.q: 怎样检查屏幕漏光？
faqs.a: 在昏暗房间以平时的亮度和观看距离显示黑色，观察边缘和角落是否有不均匀发光，不要按压面板。

faqs.q: 这个页面会关闭显示器吗？
faqs.a: 不会。它只是向显示器发送黑色像素值。需要关屏时，请使用设备电源或操作系统的休眠设置。

sections.title: Betrachtung im dunklen Raum
sections.text: Nutzen Sie die schwarze Fläche, wenn ein helles Browserfenster bei Film, Präsentation, Fotografie oder einer anderen Aufgabe bei wenig Licht stören würde. Die Pixel ändern sich, der Monitor bleibt eingeschaltet.

sections.title: Schwarzwert und Backlight-Bleeding
sections.text: Prüfen Sie in einem dunklen Raum Ecken, Ränder, wolkige Flecken und sichtbar farbige Pixel. Für mehrere Muster steht der LCD-Bildschirmtester zur Verfügung.

sections.title: Verhalten von OLED und LCD
sections.text: OLED erzeugt Schwarz durch gedimmte oder abgeschaltete Pixel. LCDs müssen eine weiterhin aktive Hintergrundbeleuchtung blockieren, weshalb Aufhellungen oder ein angehobener Schwarzwert bleiben können.

faqs.q: Spart ein schwarzer Bildschirm immer Energie?
faqs.a: Nein. Bei manchen OLED-Geräten sinkt der Verbrauch, während die LCD-Hintergrundbeleuchtung aktiv bleibt. Helligkeit, Einstellungen und die übrige Oberfläche zählen ebenfalls.

faqs.q: Wie prüfe ich Backlight-Bleeding?
faqs.a: Zeigen Sie Schwarz bei normaler Helligkeit und Entfernung in einem dunklen Raum und achten Sie auf ungleichmäßiges Leuchten an Kanten und Ecken, ohne das Panel zu drücken.

faqs.q: Schaltet diese Seite den Monitor aus?

sections.title: Nivel de negro y fuga de luz

sections.title: Comportamiento de OLED y LCD
sections.text: OLED crea el negro reduciendo o apagando píxeles individuales. LCD depende de bloquear una retroiluminación activa, por lo que puede conservar brillo o un negro elevado.

faqs.q: ¿Una pantalla negra siempre ahorra energía?
faqs.a: No. Puede reducir el consumo en algunos dispositivos OLED, mientras la retroiluminación LCD permanece activa; también influyen el brillo, los ajustes y el resto de la interfaz.

faqs.q: ¿Cómo reviso una fuga de luz?

sections.text: O OLED cria o preto reduzindo ou desligando pixels individuais. O LCD precisa bloquear uma luz de fundo ainda ativa, por isso algum brilho ou preto elevado pode permanecer.

faqs.q: Uma tela preta sempre economiza energia?

sections.title: Observation dans le noir

sections.title: Niveau de noir et fuites de lumière
sections.text: Dans une pièce sombre, observez les halos aux coins, les taches nuageuses, les fuites sur les bords et les pixels qui restent colorés. Pour plusieurs motifs, utilisez le testeur de dalle LCD.

sections.title: Comportement OLED et LCD
sections.text: L’OLED crée le noir en diminuant ou en coupant chaque pixel. Le LCD doit bloquer un rétroéclairage actif, ce qui peut laisser un halo ou un noir relevé.

faqs.q: Un écran noir économise-t-il toujours de l’énergie ?

faqs.q: Comment vérifier une fuite de rétroéclairage ?

faqs.q: Cette page éteint-elle le moniteur ?
faqs.a: Non. Elle envoie uniquement des valeurs de pixels noires. Utilisez le bouton d’alimentation ou la veille du système pour éteindre l’écran.

config.technical: This page renders the exact CSS color #00FF00, or rgb(0, 255, 0), with red and blue set to zero. Production keying may use a different green, and even lighting, exposure, camera white balance, display settings, and ambient light all affect the recorded result.

sections.title: Chroma-key setup
sections.text: Use the fullscreen field as a quick background for small objects, video-call framing, or a keyer preview. Keep the subject separated from the display and check the camera view for green spill before recording.

sections.title: Green-channel inspection
sections.text: A pure green field isolates the display's green channel, making dark, weak, or off-color areas easier to notice. Use the dedicated LCD Screen Tester for a guided multi-pattern diagnosis.

sections.title: Even coverage matters
sections.text: A usable key depends on consistent color and exposure across the frame, not maximum brightness. Check for screen reflections, hotspots, and edge falloff, then adjust the display and camera for a flatter background.

faqs.q: Is #00FF00 the standard production chroma-key green?
faqs.a: Not always. #00FF00 is exact CSS green, while studios may use a different fabric, paint, or digital key color chosen for their camera and software.

faqs.q: Can this page remove a video background?
faqs.a: No. It supplies a solid green field or PNG; background removal still happens in your camera, streaming app, or video editor.

faqs.q: Why does the green look different through my camera?
faqs.a: Camera exposure, white balance, picture profiles, display brightness, and room light can change the recorded color. The page's pixel value remains #00FF00.

sections.title: 观察深色中间调
sections.text: 较暗的紫色平场能让亮度不均、偏色斑块和突兀的色调过渡更容易看到。留意面板上是否有区域偏红、偏蓝、偏灰或接近黑色。

sections.title: 摄影和直播背景
sections.text: 把紫色用于小型主体、直播场景或墙面反光。它是氛围色，不是标准色键背景。

sections.title: 紫色与品红色的区别
sections.text: CSS 紫色 #800080 的红蓝数值为 128，而品红色 #FF00FF 的两者均为 255，后者明显更亮。需要指定色调时请核对 HEX 值。

faqs.q: 本页使用什么紫色？
faqs.a: 它使用 #800080，即 rgb(128, 0, 128)。红蓝通道数值相同，绿色为零。

faqs.q: 为什么另一台显示器上的紫色更偏蓝？
faqs.a: 面板、色温、色彩配置、亮度和环境光会改变视觉平衡。两台设备接收的像素值仍可相同。

faqs.q: 紫色适合去除视频背景吗？
faqs.a: 它不是常用的色键颜色。若工作流程需要抠像，请使用绿色或蓝色；紫色更适合作为可见背景。

faqs.q: Warum wirkt Violett auf einem anderen Display blauer?

faqs.q: Eignet sich Violett zum Entfernen eines Videohintergrunds?

sections.title: Diferencia entre morado y magenta
sections.text: El morado CSS #800080 usa rojo y azul a 128; el magenta #FF00FF los lleva a 255 y es mucho más brillante. Comprueba el valor HEX cuando necesites un tono concreto.

faqs.q: ¿Qué tono morado usa esta página?

faqs.q: ¿Por qué el morado parece más azul en otra pantalla?

faqs.q: ¿Sirve el morado para eliminar un fondo de vídeo?

faqs.q: Qual tom de roxo esta página usa?

fr.color_intro: Utilisez le champ rose comme fond doux pour des objets ou des créations. Il sert aussi de lumière d’appoint ou à comparer plusieurs écrans. Le PNG garde la même valeur pour le montage et les présentations.
fr.technical: La page affiche le rose CSS #FFC0CB, soit rgb(255, 192, 203). Dalle, température de couleur, filtres nocturnes, luminosité et lumière ambiante modifient sa teinte chaude et sa clarté. Ce n’est pas une référence calibrée.

sections.title: Fond doux et lumière d’appoint
sections.text: Le rose offre une surface claire et chaude pour l’artisanat, les produits, les diapositives et les éléments vidéo. À luminosité modérée, il peut aussi éclairer doucement un sujet proche.

sections.title: Comparer les teintes chaudes
sections.text: Affichez le même champ sur deux écrans et cherchez un glissement vers le pêche, le saumon, le magenta ou le blanc délavé. Il s’agit d’une comparaison visuelle, pas d’une calibration.

sections.title: Pas une couleur chroma key standard
sections.text: Le rose se rapproche de nombreux teints et vêtements ; le logiciel peut donc retirer une partie du sujet. Utilisez le vert ou le bleu pour le détourage.

faqs.q: Quelle nuance de rose cette page affiche-t-elle ?
faqs.a: Elle affiche le rose CSS classique #FFC0CB, soit rgb(255, 192, 203). La valeur est fixe, mais l’écran et l’environnement modifient son aspect.

faqs.q: Le rose peut-il remplacer un fond vert ?
faqs.a: Non. Le rose n’est pas une couleur chroma key standard et recoupe souvent les teintes de peau ou de vêtements.

faqs.q: Pourquoi ce rose paraît-il orange ou délavé ?
faqs.a: Une température chaude, les filtres nocturnes, une forte luminosité, la dalle et la lumière ambiante peuvent déplacer ou atténuer le rose.

config.intent_note: This is an equal-channel sRGB midpoint for flat-field inspection and neutral backdrops. It is not a physical paint swatch. It is not a calibrated 18% photographic gray card.
config.color_intro: Fill the display with solid gray to inspect broad uniformity, banding, dirty screen effect, and tint variation without the intensity of white. The same field also works as a quiet neutral backdrop, and the PNG downloads provide its exact numeric value as a file.
config.technical: All three sRGB channels are numerically equal at 128, the midpoint of the 0-255 encoded range. Because sRGB encoding is nonlinear, #808080 is not 50% display luminance, and it is not a calibrated 18% photographic gray card. Panel settings and ambient light still affect its appearance.

sections.title: Uniformity and dirty screen effect
sections.text: Mid-gray can reveal broad cloudy patches, edge shading, vertical bands, and tint changes that hide in detailed images. Inspect from a normal viewing distance, then move closer only to investigate a specific area.

sections.title: Banding and tonal behavior
sections.text: A flat field can expose abrupt bands or contours. One gray level does not replace a full gradient test. Use the LCD Screen Tester for guided grayscale and color patterns.

sections.title: Neutral UI and image backdrop
sections.text: Equal encoded red, green, and blue values provide a visually quiet background for interface mockups, screenshots, and small product images. It is neutral by numeric definition, not a guarantee of calibrated neutral appearance.

faqs.q: Is #808080 the same as an 18% gray card?
faqs.a: No. An 18% gray card is a physical reflectance reference for photography, while #808080 is the numeric midpoint of encoded sRGB values.

faqs.q: Is #808080 equal to 50% screen brightness?
faqs.a: No. sRGB values are nonlinear, so a numeric channel value of 128 does not produce half the luminance of 255.

faqs.q: What should I look for on a gray screen?
faqs.a: Look for broad streaks, cloudy patches, edge darkening, unexpected bands, or areas with a green, magenta, warm, or cool tint.

sections.title: 观察均匀性与脏屏效应
sections.text: 中灰能显示大范围云状斑块、边缘变暗、垂直条带和偏色，这些问题在复杂图像中可能不明显。先以正常距离观察，再靠近确认。

sections.title: 检查条带与色调变化
sections.text: 平场有助于发现不应出现的突兀条带或轮廓，但单一灰度不能替代完整渐变测试。需要引导式检查时使用液晶屏幕测试器。

sections.title: 中性界面与图片背景

faqs.a: 不等同。18% 灰卡是摄影用的实体反射基准，#808080 是编码 sRGB 数值的中点。

faqs.q: #808080 等于屏幕亮度的 50% 吗？

faqs.q: 灰色屏幕上应检查什么？

sections.title: Uniformität und Dirty-Screen-Effekt
sections.text: Mittelgrau macht wolkige Flächen, Randabschattung, vertikale Bänder und Farbstiche sichtbar, die in detailreichen Bildern verborgen bleiben. Beobachten Sie zunächst aus normaler Entfernung. Gehen Sie nur für einen bestimmten Bereich näher heran.

sections.title: Banding und Tonverhalten
sections.text: Eine Vollfläche kann abrupte Bänder oder Konturen zeigen, ersetzt aber keinen vollständigen Verlaufstest. Für geführte Graustufen- und Farbmuster nutzen Sie den LCD-Bildschirmtester.

sections.title: Neutrale UI- und Bildfläche
sections.text: Gleiche codierte Rot-, Grün- und Blauwerte ergeben einen ruhigen Hintergrund für Mockups, Screenshots und kleine Produktbilder. Numerisch neutral bedeutet nicht automatisch sichtbar kalibriert neutral.

faqs.q: Ist #808080 dasselbe wie eine 18%-Graukarte?
faqs.a: Nein. Eine 18%-Graukarte ist eine physische Reflexionsreferenz für Fotografie. #808080 ist der numerische Mittelpunkt codierter sRGB-Werte.

faqs.q: Entspricht #808080 halber Bildschirmhelligkeit?
faqs.a: Nein. sRGB-Werte sind nichtlinear. Ein Kanalwert von 128 erzeugt nicht die halbe Luminanz von 255.

faqs.q: Worauf sollte ich bei einer grauen Fläche achten?
faqs.a: Achten Sie auf breite Streifen, wolkige Flecken, dunkle Ränder, unerwartete Bänder sowie grüne, magentafarbene, warme oder kühle Bereiche.
